Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation at baseline was associated with a lower frequency of positive depression screen 2.5 years later in people with MS.
Sentence: "Moderate alcohol intake, being a non-smoker, diet quality, no meat or dairy intake, vitamin D supplementation, omega 3 supplement use, regular exercise, and meditation at baseline were associated with lower frequencies of positive depression-screen 2.5 years later."
Measured as: positive depression-screen (PHQ-9) at 2.5 years
Population: People living with multiple sclerosis recruited online from an international cohort
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation at baseline (self-reported, not assigned)
Comparator: No vitamin D supplementation
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 2,224
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
